content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list. Need number of CH3 groups in the compound. We need to infer from carbon shifts which correspond to methyl carbons. Typically methyl carbon shifts around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but also around 50 ppm for O-CH3 (methoxy) etc. The list: 166.40 (likely carbonyl), 131.87, 129.70, 129.70, 129.01, 129.01, 129.00 (aromatic carbons), 52.24, 43.47, 38.60. The three upfield signals likely aliphatic carbons. Which are CH3? 52.24 could be O-CH3 (methoxy) or N-CH3. 43.47 could be CH2 or CH3 attached to hetero. 38.60 similar. Need to know the structure. Not given. Could be something like methyl benzoate? That would have carbonyl (166), aromatic (6 carbons), OCH3 (52). That's one methyl. But we also have 43.47 and 38.60 maybe from other groups like CH2CH3? But no other signals. Could be a compound with three methyl groups: e.g., p-tolyl acetate? That would have carbonyl (166), aromatic (6), OCH3 (52), CH3 attached to aromatic (21). Not present. So maybe the extra signals are from CH2 groups? But we have only carbon signals, not multiplicities.

We could retrieve typical carbon shift ranges for methyl groups. Use retrieve_carbon_shifts.
